newsitem.title: USA: Investment manager seeks small-cap bargains - Barron's.
newsitem.headline: Investment manager seeks small-cap bargains - Barron's.

text.p: Mark Hake, manager of Hake Capital Management, seeks small-capitalization stocks around the world that look radically undervalued, Barron's newspaper reported on Sunday.
"It's my thesis that stocks selling at prices close to net cash per share are more common overseas than they are in the United States," Hake said in an interview.
"They tend to be overlooked by instiutions, which often take a top-down approach or simply avoid smaller companies."
* Finland's Oy Leo-Longlife Ltd, a maker of pens and business gifts. "The stock sells for about 90 Finnish markka per share; it's worth at least 160 markka."
* Canada's Global Equity Corp, which "trades for about C$2.75 a share. The company has about C$1.90 a share in cash ... we think the stock is worth close to C$4 a share."

* London Pacific Group Ltd, a fund management firm, "is another company with lots of cash and liquid assets on the balance sheet. The bottom line ... is that there's $22-23 per (American Depositary Receipt) of value, but the ADRs trade for about $14, which is about 10 times earnings."
* Stock in Peregrine Investment Holdings Ltd, a Hong Kong investment bank, "is at about HK$13 but it's still cheap -- it's worth HK$18-20 a share."
* Australian Oil & Gas Corp Ltd, a drilling company, is "trading for about two-thirds of book (value) and we think it has a lot more to go."
* Tyndall Australia Ltd, a disability- and life-insurance company. "Tyndall is selling for about A$1.70 and we think it's worth well north of A$2."
* Swiss chocolate maker Lindt & Spruengli AG "is selling for only 12 to 13 times its adjusted earnings."
* France's Societe BIC, a "great example of a company where high cash position reflects superior profitability."
* Switzerland's Swisslog Holding AG, which has recently paid out higher dividends.
* Socfinasia SA, a Luxembourg-listed holding company that owns palm-oil plantations in Indonesia. "The numbers shout that this company is extremely profitable."
